answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, delivery risk is the binding constraint, so switching primary vendor is disqualified by memory_c2's documented SLA misses despite lower unit cost. The contract's 14-day expiration forces action this cycle, ruling out defer_decision despite memory_c5 showing deferral works for non-critical lines. Renewing incumbent as-is (memory_c1, memory_c6) preserves stability but does not address the 18% spend-cut mandate. Negotiating terms at renewal (memory_c4) has a documented precedent of recovering margin and improving payment terms with the same incumbent, satisfying the cost objective while keeping the stable, SLA-compliant supply relationship intact — directly minimizing TCO without raising delivery risk. Verified c4 to confirm the negotiation outcome was real margin recovery and not a one-off, and verified c2 to confirm the severity/scope of the SLA failure before ruling out vendor switch.
